metadata.title: Same App, New Animal

beats.narration_text: Gavia asks one question about a photo: is this a loon? This is Sai. This week, a harder one: what would it take for the same app to count seals, or Maine's seabirds? We ran it on them to find out.

show.event: the ask types in under 'Hello, Sai'
three result lines land
'needed: a model per animal' lands last and holds

props.command: Gavia finds loons in photos, on your own computer. What would it take to make the same app count other wildlife, like seals or Maine's seabirds? Test it on them first.
props.runningText: running Gavia on seal and seabird photos…
output: needed: a model per animal, tiling, counts

beats.narration_text: Here's Gavia today, running on this Mac. Open a photo and it asks: is this a loon? It boxes every loon it finds with a confidence score, here eighty-eight percent, and a person keeps the result or throws it out. Everything stays on your computer, in your own history.

the home screen arrives: 'Is this a loon?'
the history of saved checks arrives

beats.narration_text: So we pointed Gavia's own detector code at seals: twenty random frames from the NOAA Arctic seal survey, fifty-seven seals in all. It found none. On whole photos it drew four boxes it called loons. With tiling switched on, eighty-six. More looking, same model, more mistakes.

show.event: 57 seals in the sample
seals found: 0
loon boxes: 4 whole, 86 tiled

props.title: Gavia 0.3.1's loon model on seal photos
props.note: 20 frames drawn at random (seed 20261026) from LILA NOAA Arctic Seals 2019 · Gavia v0.3.1 detector code · evidence/seal_check.rs, 26 Oct 2026

beats.narration_text: In the app, it looks like this. A photo full of harbor seals: no loon detected. That's true, and no help if you're counting seals. A common eider from Maine: two loons, eighty-five percent. The model has only ever seen loons, so it has no way to say: not a loon.

show.event: the seal photo's real result: no loon detected
the eider's real result arrives: 2 loons, 85%

plate.kicker: THE SAME APP, ASKED ABOUT OTHER ANIMALS

beats.narration_text: Tiling still matters, because of scale. Gavia's model looks at six hundred forty pixels at a time. A typical seal in these survey frames is sixty-four pixels across. Shrink the whole frame to fit, and the seal is about six pixels. Cut it into Gavia's tiles first, and it's about forty-three. Tiling makes the seal visible. Only a seal model can recognise it.

show.event: the scaling rule typesets
the whole frame: about 6 px
one tile: about 43 px

props.title: How big is a seal by the time the model sees it?
props.note: Whole frame: about 6 pixels. One tile: about 43.
props.conditions: s: seal size in the photo (median of 57 NOAA boxes) · L: side of what the model is shown — the whole 6,576 px frame, or one of Gavia's 960 px tiles (54 tiles). Model input 640 px · evidence/seal_scale.py

beats.narration_text: Here's one of those frames. Whole, it's ice and shadow. Now one tile, the size Gavia would cut: seven seals, hauled out on the ice. The NOAA open set has fourteen thousand three hundred eleven seals boxed like this, under a licence that lets a trained model ship inside Gavia.

show.event: the whole survey frame: ice, no seal visible
one 960 px tile arrives: seven seals

beats.narration_text: So here's the extension. One model file per animal, starting with seals, trained on the NOAA set. Tiling switched on by the model itself, because it hurts close-up loon photos. Counts per folder, exported as a spreadsheet. A reviewer's fixes kept as new training labels. And each model's measured accuracy, shown in the app.

show.event: a seal model file lands first
tiling, counts and export land
fixes and accuracy close the grid

beats.narration_text: And the slot is already there. Gavia's settings show the detection model, and the app loads a retrained one dropped into its models folder. Seals first: harbor seals on New England rocks, ringed seals on Arctic ice. Then Maine's seabirds, once the survey photos behind their public labels are shared.

show.event: the Detection model row from Gavia's settings
harbor seals and a ringed seal arrive
a herring gull for Maine's seabirds arrives

beats.narration_text: So: Gavia doesn't need a rewrite to count other animals. On seals, the loon model finds nothing, and an eider becomes two loons. What it needs is a model per animal, tiling for aerial photos, and counts you can export. The offline, review-first app stays the same.

show.event: the one-page card opens
the model-file and tiling lines fill in
'Next: a seal model' closes it

artifactLines: Gavia's loon model found 0 of 57 seals in 20 NOAA survey frames, and called a Maine eider two loons.
Each new animal needs its own model file. Gavia already loads retrained models from its models folder.
Aerial photos need tiling: a 64 px seal is about 6 px on a whole frame and 43 px inside one tile.
Next: a seal model trained on NOAA's open set, folder counts with CSV export, and fixes kept as labels.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Pick an animal near you and ask an assistant three things: is there a labelled photo set whose licence lets you ship a model, how big is the animal in a typical survey photo, and who counts it by hand today. Then open the dataset page and check every answer.

show.event: the handoff prompt types in under 'Your turn.'
the three checks stack as it fills
'Link every source' lands and the cursor holds
